claims.text: For \((r,q,i,j)=(5,6,2,2)\), the truncated Schur module has \(431\) columns and \(2130\) Pieri rows. The selected set has \(421\) Pieri rows, leaving the ten free columns \[ F_1=(22,32,33,42,43,52,44,53,54,55). \] [artifact d4c4dfff78aeadb1a178594627f0e5524df0c89072c32043e42076d86b8865d0]

Integer row reduction of the selected rows gives one unit pivot for each of the \(421\) complementary columns. Thus the \(421\times421\) complementary-column minor is unimodular, with determinant \(\pm1\). The artifact records all transformed pivot relations; in particular, \[ \begin{aligned} 221&=-32,&2211&=42,&321&=-33-42,&222&=33,\\ 22111&=-52,&2221&=-43,&3211&=43+52,&331&=-43,\\ 421&=-43-52,&322&=43,&22211&=53,&2222&=44,\\ 22221&=-54,&22222&=55. \end{aligned} \] [artifact d4c4dfff78aeadb1a178594627f0e5524df0c89072c32043e42076d86b8865d0]

The artifact’s `ALL_PIERI_REDUCTIONS` section gives an exact integral expression of every one of the \(2130\) Pieri rows as a \(\mathbb Z\)-linear combination of the \(421\) selected raw rows; its `SELECTED_RAW` section fixes the row indexing and coefficients. [artifact d4c4dfff78aeadb1a178594627f0e5524df0c89072c32043e42076d86b8865d0]

Let \(R\) be the lattice generated by all Pieri rows and \(L\) that generated by the selected \(421\) rows. The exact reductions give \(R\subseteq L\), while selection gives \(L\subseteq R\); hence \(R=L\). The unimodular complementary minor makes \(L\) a graph over the complementary columns, so \[ \mathbb Z^{431}/R\cong\mathbb Z F_1\cong\mathbb Z^{10}. \]

The second proposed family \[ F_2=(22,221,2211,222,22111,2221,22211,2222,22221,22222) \] has images \[ (22,-32,42,33,-52,-43,53,44,-54,55) \] in the \(F_1\)-basis. This is a signed permutation basis; hence \(F_2\) also is an integral basis of the quotient.
Conditional on the standard identification of this Pieri quotient with \(J_v/A_+J_v\), and on generation of \(J_v\) by each prescribed family, both families are irredundant by graded Nakayama.
